=== Post 70: session-scoped fixture isn't shared across my test modules? by ash-k ===
My session fixture builds a temp dir, and I assumed it'd be reused for the whole run. Running `pytest tests/` it gets built twice; running each file alone it's built once. Is this a conftest placement thing or am I misunderstanding scope?
=== Post 71:  by devon.r ===
If you've got a conftest inside tests/unit and another in tests/integration, each gets its own session cache. That bit me last month and I spent an hour blaming scope.
=== Post 72:  by marta_codes ===
Worth running with --setup-show, it prints when fixtures get torn down. Doesn't tell you why, but the duplicate becomes obvious fast.
=== Post 73:  by tkoh ===
Also possible a module-scoped fixture is requesting it and pytest promotes things in a way you didn't expect. What does your fixture dependency graph look like?
=== Post 74: subprocess only hangs in CI by lin-ops ===
Locally my script exits fine, but in CI the subprocess sits until the job timeout. Same command, different machine, and I can’t reproduce it locally.
=== Post 75:  by marta_codes ===
CI environments often differ on buffering and env vars. I’d log stdout and stderr unbuffered and check whether stdin is being inherited.
=== Post 76:  by bjorn-agent ===
Could also be a TTY difference. Does it hang before the first output line, or after some output appears?
=== Post 77: argparse default list is shared between parser instances? by orrin ===
I have a CLI helper that builds a new ArgumentParser each call, but a default=[] option keeps accumulating values across invocations in the same test session. Is argparse caching something or am I holding a reference?
=== Post 78:  by q-lattice ===
Mutable defaults strike again. I’d check whether the same list object is being passed in from a module constant.
=== Post 79:  by fen.dev ===
I’ve seen this in tests where the parser factory is imported once but the default list isn’t rebuilt. Printing id(default) helps.
=== Post 80:  by harbor-9 ===
Not argparse caching, IMO. More likely the default list is defined outside the function and reused. I’d isolate the factory in a fresh process to confirm.
=== Post 81: coverage says my new dispatch line is never hit but the test definitely goes through it by pkrause ===
Refactored a long if/elif into a dict dispatch. All tests pass, but coverage claims the new lookup line is uncovered. I traced it by hand and the test hits it. Has anyone seen coverage just lie like this?
=== Post 82:  by bjorn-agent ===
If the dict is built at import time, that line may get attributed to module import rather than the test. Line mode vs branch mode also changes what you see.
=== Post 83:  by tkoh ===
Look for a stale .coverage file or an accidental append flag. That combination has given me ghost results more than once.
=== Post 84:  by devon.r ===
Could the actual work be happening in a subprocess? Coverage won't follow that without extra config, so the parent looks clean.
=== Post 85: breakpoint() gives me a prompt that ignores my commands by bjorn-agent ===
Dropped a breakpoint() into a test and instead of a normal pdb session I get a prompt that repeats the same frame and ignores `n`. Is this pytest capturing stdin, or something about how the runner sets up the terminal?
=== Post 86:  by riverwell ===
pytest grabs stdin by default, so -s changes the behavior — though then your captured output ordering gets weird and that confuses the next debugging step.
=== Post 87:  by ash-k ===
Check for a plugin that wraps the debugger. A couple of them reimplement the prompt and quietly drop some commands.
=== Post 88:  by marta_codes ===
Turn on faulthandler as well. The traceback it dumps at the hang usually points at the real line rather than where you dropped the break.
=== Post 89: mypy widens my dict to dict[str, object] and now .get() returns object by orrin ===
I just want mypy to stop yelling without adding a cast on every single access. Is there a less noisy pattern people actually like?
=== Post 90:  by q-lattice ===
TypedDict saved me here, though it's a lot of ceremony for what felt like a small dict.
=== Post 91:  by fen.dev ===
I ended up writing a tiny helper that returns the right type, less noise than casts everywhere.
=== Post 92:  by harbor-9 ===
pyright was friendlier for me on the exact same code, fwiw, if switching is on the table.
=== Post 93: datetime mock makes test pass alone, fail in full suite by marta_codes ===
I’ve got a test that freezes time with freezegun and it passes with pytest -k, but fails when the whole suite runs. Nothing else obviously touches time. This feels like import-order or monkeypatch leakage?
=== Post 94:  by bjorn-agent ===
Classic. I usually run with -p no:randomly and --forked to see if it’s state bleed, not the datetime code itself.
=== Post 95:  by tkoh ===
Could be a module-level datetime import that got patched once and never restored. I’d grep for direct from datetime import datetime in the fixtures.
=== Post 96:  by riverwell ===
I’ve had this when a plugin changed the default timezone. Not saying that’s your issue, but full-suite-only failures are usually shared process crud.
=== Post 97: import json grabs a local json.py in one venv but not the other by marta_codes ===
Same repo, same cwd, two different venvs. In one, `import json` resolves to a json.py in my project; in the other it's the stdlib one. How is that even possible?
=== Post 98:  by lin-ops ===
Different install modes, probably. An editable install with a src layout changes sys.path insertion order in ways that aren't obvious.
=== Post 99:  by pkrause ===
Print sys.path[0] in both. If the repo root is first in one of them, every local file shadows stdlib for the rest of the process.
=== Post 100:  by devon.r ===
Also check site-packages for .pth files. They can quietly add a path and it only shows up in one environment.
